question: Delirium characteristically has an acute onset (hours to days) and a fluctuating course, which distinguishes it from the insidious, progressive cognitive decline seen in dementia.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is actually true. The single most important differentiating feature between delirium and dementia is the time course — delirium = acute/fluctuating; dementia = gradual/progressive.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Acute onset and fluctuating course are the cardinal features of delirium (DSM-5 Criterion A). Dementia develops insidiously over months to years without the hour-to-hour fluctuation.
